messages:
alex_g: Heads up — we've been getting reports of gRPC streaming 'stutters' from customers hitting the hosted API through the edge ALB for the last ~90m. Streams pause for ~2–7s then resume (clients see stalled tokens).
maya_s: saw it on prod-usa-west-2 too. reproducer: long-lived streaming chat, idle for ~60s, then request next chunk -> pause.
jordi_r: logs show a flurry of retransmits and HTTP/2 RST_STREAMs from the edge side. attaching tcpdump excerpt I grabbed on an affected host:
```
14:23:01.123456 IP 10.0.4.11.34256 > 3.216.14.5.443: Flags [P.], seq 345:789, ack 120, win 229, length 444
14:23:03.390000 IP 3.216.14.5.443 > 10.0.4.11.34256: Flags [.], seq 120:564, ack 789, win 0, length 444  # zero window for ~2s
14:23:05.500000 IP 3.216.14.5.443 > 10.0.4.11.34256: Flags [R.], seq 564, ack 789, win 1024, length 0
```
sean_ops: that zero-window period looks like intermediate proxy buffering/flow-control hang. which edge component sits between client and envoy? ALB -> nginx-proxy -> envoy fwd?
alex_g: topology: client -> ALB (aws) -> egress nat -> external proxy (our edge fleet) -> envoy edge -> service. But we see the same symptom when we bypass nginx-proxy (edge fleet directly behind ALB) so it's probably ALB <> edge NAT interactions.
maya_s: ALB idle timeout is 350s for http2? I thought ALB has weird keepalive behaviour on h2. if mapping gets reused after ephemeral-port churn, conntrack may hold state with a different socket.
jordi_r: checked connection stats on affected edge nodes — lots of TIME_WAIT and ephemeral port churn when autoscaler resized a few nodes earlier. Could be mapping churn + NAT translation lifetime causing packets to be dropped until kernel reestablishes.
hana_pm: we had a scaledown at 13:45 for low GPU utilization, about 12 nodes removed. Could that have pushed a bunch of streams through new egress IPs?
sean_ops: yes, that would cause source IPs to change, triggering ALB/remote peer to close and reopen streams. But we specifically see paused streams rather than immediate close. suggests path-level buffering (zero window/ stalled TX) not immediate GOAWAY.
devx: added a quick test script to reproduce — open a gRPC bidi stream, send periodic pings, then sleep 65s and send again. posted here: https://gist.github.com/devx/egress-grpc-repro. results: ~40% reproduce rate.
alex_g: can someone try toggling HTTP/2 keepalive on envoy->service side? If we send PING pings the connection might stay healthy. Not ideal as a long-term fix.
maya_s: quick experiment: increased envoy `http2_protocol_options.keepalive_interval` to 20s on one node pool — reproduction dropped to ~5% in 20m sample.
jordi_r: note: increasing keepalives adds cpu/network noise and costs, plus some customers disallow pinging. Need root fix.
sean_ops: other hypothesis: ALB uses a downstream proxy that sets WINDOW_UPDATE incorrectly when a socket migrates. Also saw a couple ALB logs with `h2_stream: stalled` earlier today. opening ticket with cloud provider.
infra_bot: [Incident] 1912301200 - edge-egress-streaming-degrade created and paged oncall.
alex_g: good. For immediate mitigation: 1) disable aggressive node scale-down for edge-nat pool for next 12h, 2) roll proxy nginx with `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1;` as a try, 3) add keepalive pings in a targeted way for high-traffic customers.
hana_pm: putting the scale-down hold in place now. also notifying SRE customers for impacted accounts.
maya_s: rolled nginx config to a canary subset (3 nodes). initial metrics: client-side stalls dropped ~60% for streams routed to canary.
jordi_r: collecting kernel conntrack dumps and iptables NAT stats from canary vs non-canary nodes. attaching snippet shows conntrack lifetime spikes around scale operations.
```
# conntrack -L | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
1200
# conntrack -L | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
8423
```
sean_ops: We should instrument mapping lifetimes and track ALB active connections. Also add tcp_info sampling in envoy to see zero-window durations.
devx: I pushed a small change to the edge e2e test harness to simulate ephemeral-port churn + scale events. will run overnight against staging.
alex_g: long term asks: (a) evaluate moving to regional EGRESS gateways with sticky eip to reduce mapping churn, (b) teach router to pre-warm NAT translations when flows move, (c) file bug with ALB provider if their h2 handling is broken.
hana_pm: adding those items to the roadmap. cost impact note: regional EIPs & bigger NAT gateways will increase monthly egress infra costs — ops team, rough ballpark?
jordi_r: rough estimate: moving to regional EIPs roughly +15% on egress infra per region. pre-warm logic is SW change, negligible infra delta. Keepalives increase CPU slightly but not costy.
sean_ops: open question: do we allow customers to opt into a "low-churn" egress plan (sticky EIP + higher cost)? could be productized.
hana_pm: noted. will loop in sales on pricing options.
maya_s: for now, keep the canary nginx change and scale-down hold. I'll monitor for 4h and then recommend next steps.
alex_g: thanks all. please paste any reproducible traces into the incident doc and link here. closing temporary pager. :thumbsup:
